Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The provided test `testLang412Left()` calls `appendFixedWidthPadLeft(null, 10, '*')` on a `StrBuilder` instance. According to the test, this triggers a failure, which the current issue report explains is due to appending a null value with fixed width causing a NullPointerException if the `getNullText()` value is not set.

Examining the implementation of `StrBuilder.appendFixedWidthPadLeft(Object obj, int width, char padChar)`, the critical line is:
```java
String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());
```
If `obj` is null, the code uses `getNullText()` to substitute the null before proceeding. The problem arises if `getNullText()` returns `null`. Then `str` is null, and subsequently, the code calls `str.length()` at line 1186, resulting in a NullPointerException.

Looking at the `StrBuilder.getNullText()` method, it simply returns a field `nullText`. If this field is not explicitly initialized or set elsewhere, it will be null, thus causing the null pointer on `str.length()`.

No relevant clues were found in recent bug reports; they are unrelated.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is that `appendFixedWidthPadLeft` does not defensively handle the case where the null text representation (`getNullText()`) is null. The method assumes `getNullText()` always returns a non-null String, leading to a NullPointerException when it actually returns null.

To fix this, the method should handle the situation where `getNullText()` returns null, for example by substituting an empty string or some default text before proceeding. Alternatively, `getNullText()` itself could default to an empty string if not set.

This explains why appending a null value with fixed width causes the observed failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
